name: Oldowan flaked stone tools in East Africa
summary: Hominins in eastern Africa struck sharp flakes from stone cores between about 3 and 2.6 million years ago, using them to butcher animals and process plants.
description: Oldowan sites at Nyayanga on the Homa Peninsula, Kenya, are dated to between 3.032 and 2.581 million years ago and include two hippopotamid butchery sites; use-wear and bone damage show the tools were used on plant and animal tissue. At Bokol Dora 1 in the Ledi-Geraru area of Ethiopia, systematically flaked stone tools are bracketed between 2.61 and 2.58 million years ago. Which hominin made them is not settled: Paranthropus teeth were found at Nyayanga, and the Oldowan is often attributed to Homo.

impact.note: Scored on the general view, not on the cited papers, that the East African Oldowan is the root from which later stone technology everywhere descends: every later human population lived by cutting tools, which changed how hominins fed themselves, and woodworking, butchery and all later toolmaking rest on it.

date.label: 3.032 to 2.581 million years ago
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Oldowan sites at Nyayanga in south-western Kenya are dated to between 3.032 and 2.581 million years ago and show hippopotamus butchery and plant processing.

evidence.supports: The 3.032-2.581 Ma Oldowan sites from Nyayanga evidence hippo butchery, plant processing, and the first Paranthropus from SW Kenya.

date.label: 2.61 to 2.58 million years ago
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: An assemblage of systematically flaked stone tools excavated in place at Bokol Dora 1, Ledi-Geraru, is bracketed between 2.61 and 2.58 million years ago.

evidence.supports: we describe a substantial assemblage of systematically flaked stone tools excavated in situ from a stratigraphically constrained context [Bokol Dora 1, (BD 1) hereafter] at LG bracketed between 2.61 and 2.58 Ma

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Lomekwi 3 in West Turkana, Kenya (about 3.3 million years ago, Harmand et al. 2015, Nature 521, 310-315): decide whether it is the first known flaked stone technology or a separate record; its status as deliberate knapping in place is debated. If it is treated as a separate concept, this record could be marked first_known.
The Nyayanga dates bracket the deposits; the sites could lie anywhere between 3.032 and 2.581 million years ago, so they are not shown to be older than Ledi-Geraru or Gona.
A published letter disputing the Ledi-Geraru date was not opened.
Whether Paranthropus or Homo made the Nyayanga tools is not settled; the paper says the Oldowan was associated with Paranthropus there.

The dataset already holds 'Gona core-and-flake stone technology' (gona-flaked-stone-cutting, concept stone-core-and-flake-knapping, 2.6-2.5 million years ago); the two concepts mean the same thing and should be joined.
The Ledi-Geraru coordinates are an approximate point for the research area, entered from memory; the Nyayanga coordinates are given in the paper (0 deg 23.909' S, 34 deg 27.115' E).

research.note: Braun et al. 2019 say systematic production of sharp-edged stone tools is unknown before the Oldowan, but the same paper notes more primitive, percussive stone tools reported from Lomekwi, Kenya, at 3.3 million years ago; the sources opened do not settle whether the Oldowan was the first flaking or a separate start.
